h: A sharp-tongued heroine and a proud landowner misjudge each other across drawing rooms; dry social comedy that slowly turns into a love story.

like.r: Same author, same matchmaking and village manners, with a heroine whose confidence is the joke and the lesson.
A lush, windswept screen version that plays up the longing between the leads and keeps the book's wit.
A modern, self-deprecating retelling of the same story, with a diary voice and a stiff, lovable Mr Darcy.

h: A confident young matchmaker keeps arranging other people's lives and misreading her own; a comedy of errors built entirely from village gossip.

like.r: Sharper romance and a more driven heroine, from the same author at her most quotable.
A funny Beverly Hills update of the same plot, with a matchmaking heroine who learns the hard way.
Another sly panorama of social climbing and marriage-market schemes, but far longer and much more cynical.

h: Two sisters, one ruled by sense and one by feeling, lose their home and their prospects and must find love on very little money.

like.r: A warm, well-cast adaptation that keeps both sisters' storylines and the book's ache over money and manners.
Another story of close sisters, poverty and first love, more homespun and more openly sentimental.
A deeper, longer study of marriage and money in provincial England, less comic and more searching.

h: A woman talked out of love at nineteen meets the man again eight years later; Austen at her most autumnal, quiet and aching.

like.r: Another restrained story of a love that duty and manners kept unspoken, with the same quiet heartbreak.
A plain-spoken heroine and a long road to the right partner, but stormier and more openly passionate.
A love thwarted by social rules, told with the same ironic eye and an even sadder sense of what was lost.

h: An orphaned governess with fierce principles takes a job at a house full of secrets; gothic romance driven by an unbending narrator.

like.r: A shy narrator, a brooding master and a mansion with a secret, rebuilt as a twentieth-century suspense story.
A short, haunting answer to Jane Eyre that tells the attic woman's story from the Caribbean.
A moody, shadowed adaptation that leans into the gothic chill rather than the romance.

h: A foundling and the girl he loves wreck two households on the Yorkshire moors; savage, stormy, and nothing like a conventional romance.

like.r: Her sister's gothic romance, with a similar wild setting but a heroine who keeps her principles and a gentler ending.
Another landscape-driven tragedy of passion and class, where the countryside seems to share the heroine's fate.
A raw, muddy, close-up adaptation that strips away costume drama and keeps the cruelty.

h: A mysterious widow moves into a ruined hall with her young son, and her diary shows what a bad marriage costs; strikingly frank for its day.

like.r: Her sister's romance of a woman who leaves a dangerous house and keeps her self-respect, with more gothic fog.
Another unhappy marriage pictured without flinching, though from the angle of a woman's desire and ruin.
A shorter, more lyrical story of a wife who refuses the role assigned to her.

h: A blacksmith's orphan receives a mysterious fortune and learns what it costs; Dickens at his most controlled, full of fog, shame and ruined rooms.

like.r: A black-and-white adaptation famous for its churchyard opening and its eerie, decaying parlor.
Another orphan climbing through class and loving someone above her station, with a gothic edge.
A far shorter story of money and ambition aimed at one unreachable person, narrated by a watcher.

h: Love, secret identity and revolution between London and Paris; Dickens at his most plotted, with one of fiction's best-known opening lines.

like.r: Another sweeping French story of revolution, sacrifice and mercy, longer and more digressive.
A faster, more swashbuckling tale of prison, disguise and a long-awaited return.
Historical fiction about power and violence at the edge of upheaval, in a cooler present-tense voice.

h: A workhouse orphan falls in with a gang of child pickpockets in grimy London; Dickens's angriest early book, equal parts melodrama and social fury.

like.r: A shadowy black-and-white adaptation that makes the criminal London of the book feel real.
A vast French counterpart about poverty, crime and mercy, with a similar mix of melodrama and moral heat.
A real childhood of hunger and hardship in Limerick, told with Dickensian humor and bitterness.

h: A boy's life from lonely childhood to adult success, crowded with Dickens's most vivid eccentrics; funny, tender and very long.

like.r: Another first-person growing-up story of cruelty at home and school, told with less comedy and more fire.
A big, humane modern novel in the same tradition of orphans, odd families and a roundabout path to adulthood.
A rival Victorian panorama with a witty narrator, though sharper and less sentimental.

h: A miser is hauled through Christmases past, present and yet to come by three ghosts; a short, vivid parable about money and kindness.

like.r: Another Christmas story of a man shown what his life has meant, with the same appeal to generosity.
A funny, surprisingly faithful retelling that keeps the ghosts and the heart and adds felt-puppet jokes.
Another Victorian moral fable with a supernatural twist, darker and aimed at vanity instead of greed.

h: A never-ending inheritance lawsuit pulls a dozen Londoners together, told by an omniscient narrator and a modest young woman in alternating chapters.

like.r: Another huge Victorian web of intersecting lives, with less fog and caricature and more moral patience.
A comparable social panorama of poverty and law, with the same mix of melodrama, mystery and protest.
A bleaker, shorter vision of an impenetrable legal system that grinds up the person caught in it.

h: A provincial town, a young idealist's disastrous marriage and a dozen interlocking lives, studied with patient intelligence; long, slow and deeply humane.

like.r: Another long novel of marriages and ideals, with a more passionate, tragic center and a Russian landscape.
A livelier, more satirical Victorian panorama of ambition and marriage.
A modern family epic with the same close attention to disappointment, marriage and inner lives.

h: A bright, headstrong girl and her beloved brother grow up beside a Midlands river and are torn apart by pride and convention; tender and devastating.

like.r: Another clever, passionate girl at odds with a narrow family, though with a more romantic route out.
A rural tragedy in which a woman's feelings meet the rules of her community, and lose.
A warmer sibling story with a similar bookish, headstrong heroine, though much gentler about family.

h: A bitter weaver hoarding gold in a village cottage has his life remade by an unexpected child; a short, warm moral fable among Eliot's novels.

like.r: Another tale of a withdrawn, money-minded man brought back to people, shorter and more openly magical.
Another English rural novel with farm labor, close villages and decency tested, with a more romantic plot.
A quiet, generous novel about grace, fatherhood and late-life tenderness.

h: A poor dairymaid is ruined by a rich man's lie and then by her community's judgment; a bleak, beautifully landscaped novel of fate and double standards.

like.r: Another story of a woman punished by a community for what a man also did, shorter and more allegorical.
Another doomed woman in a stifling provincial world, though driven by fantasy rather than by victimhood.
A slow, gorgeous adaptation that captures the book's pastoral beauty and its inexorable sadness.

h: An independent farm owner with three very different suitors, a patient shepherd and a lot of English weather; Hardy at his most romantic.

like.r: Another story of a spirited woman choosing among suitors, lighter and funnier, indoors instead of in the fields.
A heroine who insists on her independence while falling in love, with more gothic drama.
A sunlit, handsomely shot adaptation that keeps the romantic triangle and the pastoral calendar.

h: A stonemason who longs for Oxford and a cousin who defies marriage are ground down by class and convention; Hardy's bleakest novel.

like.r: Another working-class story of ambition, desire and a household pressing in on a gifted man.
Another long fall from hopes to ruin, with the same unflinching view of marriage and illusion.
A modern, suburban story of ambitions crushed by routine and a marriage that can't hold.

h: A penniless, brilliant schemer claws her way up English society while a decent girl declines; a long comic panorama narrated by a sly showman.

like.r: Another ruthless, charismatic heroine surviving by her wits through a changing world, in a lusher key.
A cool, painterly film about another charming social climber whose rise and fall is narrated with irony.
A kinder, more serious Victorian panorama of marriage and ambition.

h: A genteel southern clergyman's daughter moves to a smoky mill town and clashes with its proud manufacturer; industrial-age enemies-to-lovers.

like.r: The template for a prickly heroine and a proud man who must be corrected, in a lighter, more comic register.
A harsher, more satirical picture of the same northern industrial world and its human cost.
Another strong-minded woman and a difficult employer, with a gothic edge in place of industry.

h: Knights, outlaws and a tournament in Norman-ruled England; the swashbuckling template for later historical adventure, with some heavy 1819 prose.

like.r: Faster, wittier swordplay and court intrigue, in a style far lighter on its feet.
A modern medieval epic of rival lords, builders and a long civil war, much easier to read.
A comic fairy-tale riff on the same swashbuckling tradition, with duels, villains and winks.

h: Five aristocratic families caught in Napoleon's invasion of Russia, from ballrooms to battlefields; enormous, humane, with philosophy folded into the story.

like.r: Another huge, humane Continental epic of history, war and conscience, more melodramatic and more digressive.
A Russian epic of love and upheaval across revolution and war, lyrical and tragic.
A very long wartime saga of a family and a changing society, with a more romantic and personal focus.

h: An aristocrat's affair with a cavalry officer plays against a landowner's search for meaning; Tolstoy on marriage, society and the cost of passion.

like.r: Another married woman's doomed desire for a bigger life, tighter, colder and more ironic.
A shorter story of love running into a society's rules, with the same ruthless social detail.
A stylized, theatrical adaptation that stages the story on a literal playhouse set.

h: A conventional judge discovers he is dying and sees how thinly he has lived; a short, merciless novella that still unsettles.

like.r: A dying bureaucrat searches for meaning in the time he has left, in a humane Japanese echo of the novella.
Another short, bleak story of a man whose illness exposes his family and work life.
A quiet portrait of an ordinary academic's life and its disappointments, told with similar clear-eyed compassion.

h: A starving student kills a pawnbroker to prove a theory and is hunted by his own conscience; fevered, claustrophobic, and surprisingly gripping.

like.r: A far shorter, colder study of a killer's mind, where guilt is the question rather than the engine.
A campus group commits a murder and unravels in guilt, a modern novel in Dostoevsky's psychological mode.
A modern, polished retelling of an ambitious outsider who kills and waits for his conscience to catch up.

h: Three brothers and their monstrous father, a murder, and the century's great arguments about God and suffering; sprawling, intense, and hard to put down.

like.r: Another giant novel about God, justice and mercy, with a warmer heart and more public sweep.
A Russian satire on faith, evil and power, wilder and funnier, with a devil walking through Moscow.
A sweeping American saga of rival brothers and fathers that borrows the Cain and Abel story.

h: A bitter, brilliant civil servant rants from his basement at progress, reason and himself; a short, snarling monologue that shaped the modern antihero.

like.r: A flat, detached narrator in a different key, with the same alienation and philosophical bite.
An underground narrator speaking from a cellar, with the same sarcasm turned on American race and society.
A lonely, simmering man narrates his resentments in the city, a modern film cousin of the underground man.

h: A kind, epileptic prince returns to a cynical St Petersburg and unsettles every plan around him by being simply good; a feverish study of innocence.

like.r: Another holy fool whose sincerity collides with a hard world, in a funnier and looser form.
A comparable Russian study of love and society, calmer in style and more balanced in its view.
A short, satirical modern novel about a simple man whom everyone misreads as a sage.

h: A paroled convict, the policeman who hounds him and a Paris on the edge of revolt; giant, digressive, and built to make you cry.

like.r: Another French prisoner remade by mercy or vengeance, faster and more of a pure page-turner.
The sung-through musical on screen, with close-up live vocals that concentrate the novel's emotion.
A much shorter novel of revolution, sacrifice and love between two cities.

h: A deaf bell-ringer, a street dancer and a tormented archdeacon collide beneath the cathedral of fifteenth-century Paris; gothic melodrama with architecture as a character.

like.r: Another sympathetic outcast feared for his appearance, in a more philosophical and scientific gothic.
A disfigured outsider in love with a young singer, in a lighter pulp-gothic Paris setting.
A learned medieval mystery that treats a great building and its secrets as the main stage.

h: A wrongly jailed sailor escapes and spends years engineering the downfall of those who betrayed him; revenge as a patient, glittering machine.

like.r: Another French prison-to-redemption story, with revenge swapped for mercy and a wider social lens.
An innocent man, a patient escape and a long reckoning, told in a modern prison drama.
A much darker, more violent revenge story of a man held captive for years and obsessed with why.

h: A country boy arrives in Paris and falls in with three swordsmen over court intrigue and a queen's secret; all banter, duels and loyalty.

like.r: A darker, slower-burning Dumas adventure in which a single betrayal becomes a decade-long scheme.
An older, stiffer model of swords-and-honor adventure that Dumas lightened and sped up.
A comic tribute to swashbuckling adventure, with duels, true love and a great deal of wit.

h: A country doctor's wife feeds on romance novels and runs up debts chasing a grander life; a merciless, finely made portrait of boredom and illusion.

like.r: Another married woman in search of passion, but warmer, longer and more sympathetic to everyone involved.
A short American counterpart about a wife's desire for a life of her own.
A suburban marriage ruined by fantasies of a bigger life, with Flaubert's precise, cold gaze.

h: A carpenter's son with Napoleon fantasies schemes his way into the bedrooms and salons of the powerful; an ambitious young man's game of seduction and pride.

like.r: A comic Victorian version of the social climb, with a ruthless woman in place of a scheming young man.
Another young outsider rising through class and discovering what the climb costs.
A charming, amoral outsider insinuates himself into wealth, in a tight and cool thriller.

h: Two bored aristocrats wager on seduction and ruin, told entirely through their own letters; elegant, poisonous, and chillingly intelligent.

like.r: A sumptuous, venomous adaptation with razor-sharp performances that keeps the book's cruelty and wit.
A glossy teen update set among Manhattan prep-school elites, with the same bet and the same games.
A modern story of manipulation between two clever, ruthless partners, told with mutual deceit.

h: An optimistic young man is flung through earthquakes, wars and shipwrecks while his tutor insists this is the best of all worlds; a brisk, savage comedy.

like.r: Another bitter satire that sends an innocent traveler through absurd lands to mock human folly.
A modern absurdist satire of war and bureaucracy with the same black comic momentum.
A short, wry, fatalistic comic novel with a gentle narrator and a bitter view of war.

h: The first volume of Proust's immense study of memory and desire; sentences that run for pages and lift whole summers back into view.

like.r: A shorter modernist novel that likewise drifts through memory and perception in one flowing consciousness.
A more conventional narrative of nostalgia, class and longing for a vanished world.
A restrained memory novel in which the narrator slowly reveals what he missed.

h: A whaling captain drags his crew after one white whale; adventure, scripture, anatomy and madness piled into one enormous, strange book.

like.r: A far shorter voyage into obsession and madness, with the same brooding, symbolic grandeur.
A tense modern sea hunt for a monstrous fish, with an obsessed seafarer at its center.

like.t: The Old Man and the Sea
like.r: A spare, short story of one man's duel with a great fish, with none of Melville's digressions.

h: A schemer of a boy dodges school, whitewashes a fence and stumbles into a murder case in a sleepy river town; sunlit nostalgia with real menace underneath.

like.r: Another small Southern town seen through a child's eyes, with a heavier moral center.
A film about boyhood friendship and a summer adventure, equally nostalgic and darker at the edges.
A boy's adventure of maps, pirates and growing up quickly, with more swashbuckle and less small-town comedy.

h: A runaway boy and an escaped slave drift down the Mississippi on a raft; a comic, vernacular adventure that becomes a hard look at American conscience.

like.r: Another child's moral awakening about racism in the South, gentler in tone and more courtroom-focused.
A teenager's distinctive, rambling voice again carries the book, with city loneliness replacing the river.
A comic Southern picaresque with an eccentric voice and a great deal of social satire.

h: A Puritan town brands a woman for adultery and keeps its own sins hidden; short, severe, allegorical, and still cutting about shame.

like.r: A play about the same Puritan culture of accusation, panic and hypocrisy, with sharper pacing.
Another woman judged by her community for what a man did, in a pastoral English setting.
A modern dystopia built on Puritan control of women's bodies and shame.

h: A wife and mother on the Louisiana Gulf coast starts to want a life of her own; a short, sensuous novel that scandalized its first readers.

like.r: A longer, colder look at a wife whose longing leads her out of marriage.
A shorter and more terrifying story of a woman confined by the roles prescribed for her.
A flowing portrait of a woman's inner life under social pressure, more modernist and more elliptical.

h: A woman confined to an upstairs nursery for her rest cure becomes obsessed with the wallpaper; a short, claustrophobic descent told in diary-like entries.

like.r: Another slow psychological haunting in which the house and the narrator's mind blur together.
Another woman defying the roles set for her, with a quieter, more sensual tone.
A longer, sharper account of a woman's mental breakdown in a world that wants her docile.

h: A pampered dog is stolen and sold into Yukon sled teams, where hardship strips him back to instinct; a short, brutal adventure from the dog's side.

like.r: A true story of a young man in the wilderness, with the same pull of freedom and the same cost.
A short, tough survival story of a boy alone in the woods.
Another story of animals struggling for survival, with a heavier mythology and group of heroes.

h: A sentimental, crusading novel built from separated families, cruel owners and an enslaved man's patient faith; melodramatic, direct, and written to be felt.

like.r: A later, more fragmentary and haunting novel about slavery's afterlife in a family.
A true narrative by a free man sold into bondage, plainer and more shocking for being real.
A comic and vernacular book that confronts slavery through a boy's conscience.

h: A beautiful young man wishes to stay young while his portrait ages in his place; epigram-studded decadence slowly curdling into horror.

like.t: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
like.r: Another Victorian novella about a respectable man and his hidden self, shorter and more fast-moving.
A modern story of beautiful, privileged people and the moral rot beneath their refined talk.
A lush, decadent gothic narrated by an immortal who weighs beauty against cost.

h: Two men invent alter egos to escape duty and court women, and the lies pile up; a farce in which every line is polished into an epigram.

like.r: Another sparkling comedy of manners and class, with more argument and a sharper social point.
A later drawing-room comedy in the same vein of brittle wit, with a ghost in the marriage.
A novel of the same polished social comedy, with marriage plots and a heroine with a quick tongue.

h: An independent American heiress inherits a fortune in Europe and is courted by people with plans for it; a slow, subtle novel about choice and being used.

like.r: A clearer, more compact novel of social cages and thwarted choices in a James-like world.
Another young woman's bad marriage, with more breadth and more moral heat.
A dreamy, offbeat adaptation that lets the heroine's inner life spill into the images.

h: A governess alone with two children at a remote estate sees figures no one else admits to seeing; a ghost story that may be a mind coming apart.

like.r: A later ghost story with the same question of whether the haunting is real or in the heroine's mind.
A beautifully eerie black-and-white adaptation that keeps the ambiguity and the sense of dread.
Another young woman alone in a great house where something unseen presses on her.

h: A New York lawyer engaged to the perfect girl falls for her outcast cousin; a Gilded Age love story where the cruelest weapon is good manners.

like.r: An opulent adaptation in which every glance, dinner and glove carries the story's repression.
A denser, more abstract look at similar social traps and the women caught in them.
A later New York novel of longing and class, shorter, flashier and more lyrical.

h: A poor farmer, his sickly wife and her lively cousin share one snowbound Massachusetts farmhouse; a brief, icy tragedy of duty and missed chances.

like.r: Another bleak love triangle in a hard landscape, with more violence and a wider cast.
A longer, equally fatalistic rural tragedy where weather and poverty close in on love.
A quiet, patient novel of a small American community, far more gentle in its end.

h: A riverboat captain steams up the Congo toward a legendary ivory agent; a short, murky voyage into empire's greed and what it does to those who profit.

like.r: Transplants the river journey to the Vietnam War, keeping the descent into madness and moral murk.
A novel of colonialism from the African side, often read as an answer to Conrad.
A family's mission to the Congo, with a long view of arrogance, faith and the aftermath of empire.

h: One ordinary Dublin day in 1904 refracted through a dozen styles; funny, filthy, baffling and rewarding, best taken with a guidebook and company.

like.r: A far shorter, gentler single-day city novel that flows through many minds in a similar way.
A modern maximalist monster that likewise rewards patience with jokes, digressions and big feeling.
Another encyclopedic, difficult, funny novel that tests the reader and pays them back.

h: Fifteen precise stories of ordinary Dubliners, from boyhood to death, each stalled in some small paralysis; plain on the surface, devastating underneath.

like.r: A linked set of small-town portraits with the same quiet sadness and spare surface.
Linked stories about a community and its disappointments, told with similar compassion and restraint.
A tender, faithful film of the collection's final story, a winter party that turns inward.

t: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
h: Stephen Dedalus grows up in Catholic Ireland and breaks from church, nation and family to become a writer; the prose matures with him.

like.r: Another autobiographical coming-of-age story of a gifted boy, a family and a break with home.
A teenage rebel's voice and alienation, more colloquial and far less formal.
A sharp, autobiographical novel of a young artist's struggle to become herself.

h: A London hostess prepares a party while a shell-shocked veteran walks the same streets; a single day told through drifting minds, flowing like music.

like.r: A modern novel that answers Woolf directly, braiding three women's days across the century.
The great single-day novel of Dublin, wilder, funnier and much harder.
A modern English novel with flowing interior perspectives and a melancholy sense of time.

h: A family and its guests at an island summer house, before and after the war; time passes in the gaps between thoughts.

like.r: Her more urban, party-bound novel of consciousness, a little more plot and a little more tension.
A quiet, luminous novel of family loss and drifting time, in a very different American landscape.
Another English novel of memory and regret told in elegant, restrained prose.

h: Woolf asks why women wrote so little fiction and answers with a wandering, witty lecture about money, rooms and the freedom to think.

like.r: A much longer, denser philosophical account of how women are made secondary.

like.t: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
like.r: The older foundational argument for women's education and independence, more formal and fiery.
A short, modern, conversational essay on the same questions, easy to finish in an evening.

h: A young nobleman lives four centuries and wakes one morning as a woman; a playful mock-biography and love letter to English literature.

like.r: A sumptuous, witty adaptation with Tilda Swinton that keeps the book's lightness and time-hopping.
A big, funny modern novel about gender and family history across generations.
A science-fiction exploration of gender and identity, calmer and more serious.

h: A bank clerk is arrested one morning for a crime no one will name and sinks into an endless, airless bureaucracy; nightmare logic played deadpan.

like.r: A fuller, more political vision of a system that watches and punishes without explaining itself.
A darkly comic, visually wild film about paperwork turning into a trap.
Another man judged by a system that cares little for the truth of his life, in a plainer voice.

h: A traveling salesman wakes up as a giant insect and his family must live with it; a short, deadpan nightmare about work, shame and being useful.

like.r: Another short, strange, detached story about a man at odds with the world around him.
A body-horror film in which a man's transformation turns into slow tragedy.
Another voice of an alienated, bitter man, more talkative and more openly furious.

h: A land surveyor summoned to a village can never reach the castle that hired him; an unfinished, endlessly looping fable of bureaucracy.

like.r: His other unfinished-feeling masterwork of bureaucracy, tighter and more menacing.
A spare play of waiting and futility with the same absurd comedy and unanswered questions.
A modern allegory of social collapse told with the same plain voice and relentless logic.

h: A mysterious millionaire's lavish parties are all aimed at one woman across the bay, seen by a watchful neighbor; short, glittering, and aching.

like.r: A bleaker look at the American dream through a suburban marriage in slow collapse.
Another narrator dazzled by a glamorous world and its beautiful, doomed inhabitants.
A pop-flashy, maximalist adaptation with modern music and parties that go for pure spectacle.

h: An American psychiatrist and his rich, fragile wife drift along the French Riviera as the glamour wears thin; Fitzgerald's longer, sadder, more personal novel.

like.r: His shorter, tighter book, with the same glitter and doom at a faster pace.
Another novel of expatriates drinking through the 1920s, in a much sparer prose.
A short, sun-bleached French Riviera novel of privilege, boredom and consequence.

h: Aimless expatriates drink their way from Paris cafes to the bullfights of Pamplona; terse, restless, and haunted by what the war did to them.

like.r: A looser, jazzier novel of restless friends drifting from place to place, with a later generation's energy.
A contemporary of Hemingway's novel, more lyrical and more romantic about the same lost era.
His memoir of 1920s Paris, with the same café life and the same plain, clear sentences.

h: An American ambulance driver falls for an English nurse on the Italian front; love and retreat told in short, hard sentences that hold back the feeling.

like.t: All Quiet on the Western Front
like.r: The German side of the same war, more focused on trench life and its numbing losses.
A lyrical wartime love story, more fragmented and more poetic than Hemingway's plain style.
A bigger, more poetic love story set against the chaos of war and revolution.

h: An American dynamiter joins a guerrilla band in the Spanish Civil War with a bridge to blow in three days; a tight war novel about ideals and fear.

like.r: A first-hand account of the same war and its political confusion, plainer and more disillusioned.
A dark fairy tale set in the aftermath of the Spanish Civil War, mixing brutality with fantasy.
A more lyrical love story set in the middle of revolution and civil war.

h: Four sections, four minds, one decaying Southern family; the first narrator can't tell time and the book dares you to keep up.

like.r: His other great Southern family tragedy, built on competing tellers and a buried past.
Another novel of flowing consciousness and time shifts, gentler and more accessible.
A hauntingly fractured novel about family, memory and the South's wounds.

h: A poor Mississippi family hauls its mother's coffin across the county to bury her, in fifty-nine monologues, some tragic and some very funny.

like.r: Another poor family on a long, hard journey, told in a broader and more political register.
A bleak journey with a dead-calm, stripped-down style and a family at the center.
A short Southern Gothic novel with grotesque comedy and a harsh view of faith.

h: A pregnant drifter, a disgraced preacher and a man whose race the town can't settle meet in one Mississippi summer; dense, tragic, and more plotted than Faulkner's reputation.

like.r: A gentler and more accessible novel about race and violence in a Southern town.
A harder-edged, faster novel of race, fear and a young man's fate in America.
A haunting novel that likewise treats the South's racial legacy with lyrical intensity.

h: A dispossessed Oklahoma farm family drives west to California in a battered truck and finds no welcome; angry, humane, with interludes that widen the lens.

like.r: A stark, classic black-and-white adaptation with Henry Fonda that distills the road and the anger.
A modern film of economic drifters on the American road, quieter and more meditative.
Another protest novel about the working poor, more focused on one family and more graphic.

h: Two migrant ranch hands share a dream of their own patch of land; a short, plain-spoken book that builds to heartbreak with no wasted line.

like.r: Another American classic about empathy, injustice and prejudice, with a child's perspective.
A short, grim story of how people behave when civilization falls away.

like.t: The Old Man and the Sea
like.r: Another very short, spare novel of dignity and loss told with the same plainness.

h: A Florida woman recounts three marriages and her slow claiming of her own voice; warm vernacular dialogue and lush imagery, rooted in all-Black towns.

like.r: Another Black Southern woman finding her voice through hard relationships, told in letters and dialect.
A darker, more haunted novel about Black womanhood and memory.

like.t: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
like.r: A memoir of growing up in the segregated South, with the same lyrical voice and resilience.

h: A young Black man in 1930s Chicago takes a job with a wealthy family and one night's fear sets off a catastrophe; a furious, gripping tragedy.

like.r: A wider, more surreal and ironic novel of a Black man's place in American life.
A modern nonfiction letter about race, fear and the body in America.
An older novel of a murderer's mind and the pressures that shape him, with more philosophy.

h: A headstrong Georgia belle fights to survive the Civil War and Reconstruction while pining for the wrong man; huge, romantic, and contested for its view of the antebellum South.

like.r: The Technicolor epic that made Scarlett and Rhett iconic, with sweeping sets and melodrama.
An older, more satirical portrait of a ruthless woman who will do anything to rise.
A shorter, moodier romance that centers a great house and a love tangled with the past.

h: A Nebraska boy remembers the Bohemian immigrant girl he grew up beside on the prairie; plainspoken, elegiac, and full of weather and land.

like.r: A quiet, reflective Midwestern novel of memory and grace in a similar plain, luminous voice.
A spare, lyrical novel set in an American landscape, strange and more haunting.
A larger and angrier novel of ordinary Americans on the land and the forces that uproot them.

h: A Lithuanian immigrant family is ground up by Chicago's meatpacking yards; fiction as muckraking, with scenes that still turn stomachs.

like.r: Another protest novel of the laboring poor, with a larger canvas and more lyrical compassion.
A nonfiction investigation that revisits the meatpacking industry's conditions a century later.
A journalist's first-hand report on low-wage work, with the same anger at the system.

h: A tidy future of engineered castes, free pleasure and happy conformity, with one outsider who refuses it; a dystopia where control comes as comfort, not fear.

like.r: The opposite dystopia, where control comes through fear and surveillance instead of pleasure.
A shorter, more lyrical dystopia about a society that numbs itself with entertainment and burns books.
A quiet, devastating novel of a managed society and the people it quietly uses.

h: A minor party clerk keeps a secret diary under a regime that watches, rewrites history and polices thought; bleak, lucid, and unnervingly familiar.

like.r: A faster and more poetic dystopia about burning books and the state's use of distraction.
A dystopia of control and surveillance seen from a woman's inner view, with a similarly cold clarity.
A satirical, visually wild take on a bureaucratic state that crushes its dreamers.

h: Farm animals overthrow their owner and slowly rebuild the tyranny they fled; a short fable that explains power by letting you watch it happen.

like.r: Another short, bleak parable of how a group builds and breaks its own order.
A satirical dystopia about how power keeps the governed docile, with pleasure instead of fear.
A tense, grown-up novel about a revolutionary trapped by the system he helped build.

h: A shy bride arrives at Manderley and finds the first Mrs de Winter still rules it; a first-person gothic of insecurity, jealousy and a very big house.

like.r: The original shy-heroine-in-a-secret-house story, with a stronger-willed narrator.
A glossy, suspenseful black-and-white version that makes the house and its housekeeper truly frightening.
A slow, class-conscious ghost story set in a decaying English country house.

h: An Oxford friendship leads a middle-class narrator into a fading Catholic aristocratic family; elegiac, ornate, and soaked in longing for a vanished world.

like.r: Another outsider narrator under the spell of glamorous people and a lost golden age.
A modern, darker story of an outsider drawn into a beautiful, closed circle.
A quieter novel of a vanishing English household and a narrator's regrets.

h: A miner's son in the Nottinghamshire coalfields is torn between his possessive mother and the women he loves; intimate, earthy, and unsparing about family.

like.r: A working-class young man's ambition and desire ground down by convention, bleaker still.

like.t: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
like.r: Another autobiographical coming-of-age novel of a boy breaking from family, but more formal and cerebral.
A warmer, more nostalgic novel of a Welsh mining family and a changing community.

h: A wealthy, paralyzed baronet's wife and the estate gamekeeper begin an affair; frank for its date, and as concerned with class and industry as with sex.

like.r: A colder, earlier novel about a married woman's hunger for passion and its consequences.
A grander novel of adultery, society and the cost of following desire.
A lyrical, sensual novel of love and wounded bodies, more fragmented and wartime.

h: An accusation in the Marabar Caves splits British and Indian friends in the Raj; a slow, ambiguous study of empire where nothing quite resolves.

like.r: A vibrant, magical-realist novel of India across Independence, loud where Forster is cool.
A harsher, more sardonic picture of British colonial society and its cruelty.
A sweeping, scenic adaptation that carries the cave sequence's mystery.

h: A detached Algiers clerk attends his mother's funeral, drifts through a summer and commits a crime he can't explain; flat, sunlit, unsettling.

like.r: Another French existentialist novel of a man estranged from the world, more internal and diary-like.
The opposite temperament, a seething, talkative narrator with the same alienation.
A man put on trial by a world that cares little for the truth of his life.

h: A plague seals the Algerian port of Oran and its doctors, priests and clerks respond in different ways; a calm, grave allegory that reads differently in an epidemic.

like.r: A bleaker, stranger allegory of an epidemic that exposes how a society behaves under pressure.
A humane modern novel of a pandemic world, more hopeful and more art-minded.

like.t: A Journal of the Plague Year
like.r: A fictional eyewitness account of London's plague, closer to reportage.

t: All Quiet on the Western Front
h: A German schoolboy-turned-soldier tells the trench war in plain, numb detail, between mud, rats and the comrades he loses; short, harrowing and humane.

like.r: The same war from the Italian front, with a love story and a dryer style.
A stranger, wryer novel about another war's horror, told with time shifts and dark humor.
A bitter film about the cruelty of command in the trenches of the First World War.

h: A brahmin's son leaves home to seek enlightenment through asceticism, pleasure and the river; a short, luminous parable of finding meaning by living.

like.r: A simpler, more fable-like quest for meaning, with a similar gentle, spiritual tone.
A short book of lyrical wisdom on love, work and death, more aphoristic than narrative.

like.t: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
like.r: A road-trip philosophical novel that likewise treats meaning as a way of living.

h: A poet is led through Hell, Purgatory and Heaven by Virgil and Beatrice; part theology, part score-settling, with some of poetry's most vivid imagery.

like.r: Another epic poem of sin, fall and cosmic order, more dramatic and more Protestant.
A verse drama of a restless scholar's bargain, with a similar metaphysical scope and pull.
A satirical modern novel with a devil, a moral journey and a long literary memory.

h: A gentleman reads so many chivalry romances he rides out as a knight with a farmer for a squire; a long, funny book about illusions that turns tender.

like.r: Another early comic novel that plays with its own form, digresses endlessly and delights in it.
A short, quick satire of a naive hero wandering through a hard world.
A modern comic picaresque about a delusional hero tilting at the world.

h: A prince is told by his father's ghost to avenge a murder and can't stop thinking; a tragedy of doubt, madness and a rotten court.

like.r: A comic, absurdist play that views Hamlet's events from the sidelines, through two minor characters.
A family-friendly animated retelling that keeps the murdered king, the exiled prince and the uncle.
A faster, bloodier tragedy of ambition and guilt, with a less introspective hero.

h: A general hears a prophecy and murders his way to the throne with his wife's urging; one of the shortest, fastest tragedies, soaked in blood and guilt.

like.r: A samurai retelling set in feudal Japan, all fog, ghosts and fate.
A stark black-and-white adaptation that stages the play like a nightmare.
A longer, more reflective tragedy of a prince, ghosts and revenge.

h: Two teenagers from feuding families fall in love within a week of duels and secret vows; the original star-crossed romance, lyrical and fast.

like.r: A musical retelling in 1950s New York, with gang rivalry in place of family feuds and glorious songs.
A pop-fueled, gun-toting adaptation that keeps Shakespeare's language in a modern Verona Beach.
Another doomed, all-consuming love across a family feud, much darker and more vengeful.

h: A general is poisoned toward jealousy by his own ensign with a handkerchief and a rumor; a tragedy of manipulation where the villain explains little.

like.r: A modern thriller in which a charming schemer manipulates everyone around him.
A marriage twisted by lies and performed emotion, with a quiet, calculating sense of control.
Another short, fast tragedy driven by a single corrupting idea and a lethal spouse.

h: A Norwegian wife with a secret debt plays the pet to her husband until the truth walks in; a living-room drama whose final scene shocked Europe.

like.r: A short novel of a wife who starts to want more than her role, in a more sensual register.
A tighter, more terrifying story of a woman confined by a husband's kindly control.
Another claustrophobic domestic drama in which truth and illusion collide.

h: A fading Southern belle moves into her sister's cramped New Orleans flat and collides with her brutish brother-in-law; heat, desire and cruelty in one room.

like.r: Another American family tragedy built on illusions that collapse, with a stronger social angle.
A savage night of marital warfare and game-playing in a single living room.
A modern film that updates the same fallen-socialite story, with the same unraveling.

h: An aging traveling salesman loses his grip on the present, and on the American promise he sold his sons; memory and reality blur on stage.

like.r: A lusher, more poetic American tragedy of illusions meeting reality.
A harder, funnier play about salesmen under pressure, with profane rhythms.
A novel about the same suburban dream curdling, with a couple in place of a salesman.

h: A phonetics professor bets he can pass a flower girl off as a duchess by fixing her accent; class comedy in rapid talk with a prickly, unsentimental edge.

like.r: The big musical version, with songs and costumes that sweeten the play's sharper edge.
Another sparkling comedy of manners where wit and class collide, lighter on argument.
A novel about another well-meaning meddler remaking someone else's life, with a gentler heart.
